root_idea.summary: The root's central semantic orientation is worship, devotion, and taking a being as an object of worship; إِلٰهٌ is therefore a deity or object of worship, while اللّٰهُ is the proper name of the one true God.
root_idea.development: The lexical system develops from worship and devotional practice to the deity or divinity associated with worship. Lane also records branches of seeking refuge, protection, and remaining in a place; the confusion and perplexity branch is explicitly related to وَلِهَ and is treated separately by the root evidence.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized citation form إِلَٰه.
Displayed as the distinct proper name ٱللَّه.
Displayed separately because اللّٰهُمَّ is a fixed vocative form with its own Quranic occurrences and lexical behavior.

senses.definition: A deity or object of worship; a god, including a claimed or false god and, in the plural, a group of gods or idols.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for whatever is treated as an object of worship. The plural آلهة is used for multiple deities and is often applied polemically to idols or other rejected objects of worship.

senses.definition: The God, the one true deity.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in constructions that identify God as the sole deity, including expressions such as “your God,” “our God,” and “there is no deity but Him.” This sense is a contextual specification of the deity notion rather than a separate inflectional form.

senses.definition: Allah; the proper name of the one true God.
senses.usage_conditions: The name is used as a proper name and is not restricted by case or by the prepositions and particles that precede it. In the Quranic formula إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ, it expresses belonging to God and eventual return to Him, especially in response to affliction.

senses.definition: O Allah; a fixed vocative form used in addressing God.
senses.usage_conditions: This form functions as a vocative and is distinct from ordinary case-inflected uses of ٱللَّه.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal-noun usage. A reported Quranic variant at 7:127 reads إِلَاهَتَكَ, “your worship or service,” rather than the canonical reading آلهتك, “your gods.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become confounded or perplexed and unable to see the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This branch is reported as originally related to وَلِهَ and is distinguished from the worship branch in the root-level evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become vehemently impatient or grieved on account of someone, or to manifest intense grief and agitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs with عَلَى in the construction أَلِهَ عَلَى فُلَانٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek refuge, protection, aid, or succour from someone; to have recourse to someone for preservation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs with إِلَى in the construction أَلِهَ إِلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, stay, abide, or dwell in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs with بِ in the construction أَلِهَ بِالْمَكَانِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To protect, shelter, preserve, rescue, aid, or deliver someone from harm; to render someone safe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative transitive construction describing the granting of refuge or security.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Making someone serve or worship; enslaving or subjecting someone to service.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II verbal noun associated with causing service, worship, or enslavement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reckon someone among the gods, regard someone as a god, or make someone a god.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported additional use of the Form II verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To devote oneself to religious services or exercises and apply oneself to acts of devotion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V devotional usage describing sustained religious practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Godship, divinity, or the state of being divine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun denoting divinity or godship, distinct from the action of worship itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A goddess; in particular, a serpent or great serpent in an archaic lexical usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine lexical branch associated with objects once treated as objects of worship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The moon or the new moon, when termed هِلَال.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An archaic usage connected with the worship or veneration of the heavenly body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sun, including the hot sun.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An archaic usage connected with the honor or worship accorded to the sun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Divine, theological, or relating to God or a god.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributive adjective used of matters belonging to divinity or theology.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Theology: the study of God's being and attributes and of religious doctrines.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical abstract noun for the theological discipline.

other_classical_meanings.definition: God, invoked in an oath: “by God.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in oath formulas such as ٱللَّهِ لَأَفْعَلَنَّ and related elliptical constructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An expression attributing excellence or a praiseworthy deed to God, hence expressing admiration: “how excellent” or “divinely gifted.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in formulas such as لِلَّهِ دَرُّكَ and لِلَّهِ أَنْتَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An emphatic expression meaning “unless indeed” or “unless possibly.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use of اللهمَّ in an exception or qualification.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An emphatic expression meaning “yes indeed” or “yea, verily.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a corroborative response to an interrogative, especially in the formula اللهمَّ نَعَمْ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Inflectional and conjugational information without an independent gloss.
Worship or service, including the reported Quranic variant.
Remaining or dwelling in a place.
Primary-signification clarification covered by the service and worship meaning.
Reported sense of reckoning someone a god.
Deity meanings and distinct archaic feminine lexical branches.
Inflectional pointer to the Form I verbal noun.
Proper-name meaning, Quranic belonging formula, oath use, and admiration formulas.
Vocative Allahumma and its additional idiomatic uses.

cautions: The reported reading إِلَاهَتَكَ at 7:127 means “your worship or service”; the canonical QAC occurrence is the common reading آلهتك, “your gods.” The variant is therefore preserved as a distinct lexical item rather than silently assigned to the public headword إِلَٰه.
The derivation and historical analysis of ٱللَّه are disputed in the lexical sources; the Quranic form is presented securely as a proper name regardless of that derivational disagreement.
The confusion and perplexity branch is explicitly associated with وَلِهَ in the supplied evidence and should not be treated as the root's central worship meaning.
